newsitem.title: MEXICO: More Mexico banks may sell past-due loans to gov't.
newsitem.headline: More Mexico banks may sell past-due loans to gov't.

text.p: At least five more Mexican banks will need to sell some of their past-due loans to the government's Fobaproa fund established to improve the capitalization of banks, the government news agency Notimex reported on Wednesday.
Eleven banks have had to pass on part of their loan portfolio to Fobaproa since 1995, according to a report by the National Bank and Securities Commission (CNBV).

The Notimex report identified Banco del Atlantico, Banco Mexicano and Banoro as three of the banks that might need help from Fobaproa this year because of a high proportion of past-due loans to capital.
"It will probably be those banks and some others that need to achieve a minimum of capitalization," one source at CNBV told Reuters on condition of anonymity.
All Mexican banks pay dues to Fobaproa, which has increasingly come to the aid of lending institutions since the economic crisis which began in December 1994.
